correctness.rationale: For unit-rate symmetric k-exclusion, tilted generator L_z=e^z B-diag(q) with B1=q; reversible finite-state eigenvalue perturbation gives asymptotic variance/T = mu+2<q-mu,(-L)^+(q-mu)>_pi, with positive form equality iff q(S) constant. A constant total exit intensity gives exponential IID holding times, hence a homogeneous Poisson counting process from any initial state. For 2<=k<=N-2, swapping two vertices in equal-size cuts forces A_uw-A_vw=c_uv for all other w and (N-2k)c_uv=0. If N!=2k, connectedness forces K_N; for N=2k the nonzero row-difference case yields a balanced star, the only connected alternative. For k=1 or N-1 any regular graph works. Independent exact enumeration of every connected labelled simple graph on 4,5,6 vertices recovers only the asserted interior equality cases (4: four labelled stars plus K4; 5: only K5 for k2 and k3; 6: six labelled stars plus K6 at k3).
residual_risks: The strict Fano gap is long-time stationary, not a uniform finite-T lower bound.
Weighted, directed, disconnected networks and rejected attempts are not covered.
